description: We are Pyromancer, a team of two: Alicia, who works on machine learning and scientific software, and Paloma, a psychologist that will work on human-computer interaction and human factors. Alicia builds the SI and data pipeline. Paloma makes sure the dashboard fits how researchers and engineers actually think and decide, keeping information clear, cognitive load low and insights ready for operational use. Science and human-centered design, so no knowledge is lost among a sky of information.
summary:
Flame Waypoint is a discovery tool for NASA's microgravity combustion data. Decades of fire experiments are spread across the Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository, test spreadsheets and technical papers, each in a different format. That makes it hard for engineers to answer a simple question: has anyone tested fire in the atmosphere we plan to use?

We built a pipeline that gathers 24 PSI combustion investigations and their NASA papers. It turns 1,681 test records into one consistent dataset of oxygen, pressure, flow and fuel. A local open-weights LLM extracts findings from the papers, and every value stays linked to its source sentence. An interactive dashboard ranks experiments by how close they are to the ISS, a Moon base, a pressurized rover or Mars. It also maps which conditions have and have not been tested; few tests reach the Moon base requirement of ≥ 30 % O₂ at ≤ 10.2 psi. An offline assistant answers questions in natural language and cites its sources.

Everything runs without an internet connection, and we measured its energy cost so it could run on board. Fire is one of the most serious risks in space. Flame Waypoint helps crews and engineers make design decisions from evidence and shows where new experiments are needed.
details:
Our Python pipeline downloads 24 combustion investigations and finds the NASA papers behind them. It reads 1,681 test records from the PSI test files directly, without SI. A local open-weights model (mistral-nemo, run with Ollama) then extracts fuels, conditions and findings from the papers. Every value has to match the sentence it came from, or it's rejected.

The dashboard lets engineers:

- rank experiments by how close they are to a target atmosphere (ISS, Moon base, rover, Mars or a custom one);

- see on a map which oxygen and pressure conditions have never been tested;

- compare experiments side by side;

- ask questions in plain language and get answers that cite their sources.

The benefit is speed and trust. In seconds you can see what evidence exists for your mission, and every number links back to a NASA source. It also shows where new experiments are needed. For example, very few tests reach the Moon base requirement of ≥ 30 % O₂ at ≤ 10.2 psi.

We chose to run everything offline, so a crew could use it without a link to Earth, and we estimated the energy cost of running it on board. We also didn't want the SI to have the last word, since it is of non-deterministic nature. The numbers are computed in Python and the model only puts them into words.

We developed SI agentic tools in Python to power the local model because we believe that independence is crucial for space missions and also organizations such as NASA. There is also the security factor, where no data is uploaded to the cloud and is kept private.

Built with Python (standard library only), Ollama, plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and GitHub Pages and Actions, which run 61 automated tests on every deploy. We developed it on an Apple M3 Pro, with Claude as a coding assistant.
